title: Love Island USA, season 2 episode 20: attention after recoupling
inspected: Full episode transcript, opening morning conversation about time together after the recoupling.
finding: A complaint about not getting one-on-one time is rehearsed with a friend first; the speaker simultaneously praises her new partner and asks for attention, while the friend briefly jokes about neediness.
quote: BUT LET ME SPEND TIME WITH HIM.
label: Evidence
writer_takeaway: Let a partner test a complaint with a friend and qualify it before saying what they want.
limitations: Edited reality TV, not spontaneous continuous conversation; transcript has all-caps text, garbled names, and weak speaker attribution.

title: Love Island USA, season 2 episode 20: asking for a one-on-one chat
inspected: Full episode transcript, Aaron requesting a private conversation with Sher and discussion of other connections.
finding: The invitation happens publicly, includes a joking refusal and reassurance from the current partner, then shifts to banal questions about work and life goals before romantic availability is probed.
quote:
I WANTED TO TALK TO YOU ONE-ON-ONE.
HOW DO YOU FEEL?
label: Evidence
writer_takeaway: Start a romantic check-in with logistical permission and ordinary questions rather than an immediate confession.
limitations: Edited broadcast conversation; all-caps transcript may collapse speakers and omit pauses.

title: Too Hot to Handle, season 3 episode 3: morning-after rule-breaker banter
inspected: Full transcript, opening group breakfast exchange about sleeping arrangements and kissing penalties.
finding: A group turns an evasive answer into escalating concrete questions, repeat-back, a pillow joke and small overlapping echo reactions; confessional explanation is intercut, not part of the breakfast conversation.
quote:
Where'd it go?
It found some legs and just crawled out.
label: Evidence
writer_takeaway: For group teasing, let several people pursue one small factual detail rather than giving everyone a polished comeback.
limitations: Edited reality TV; music, narrator, confessionals, and unsignaled speaker changes interrupt the subtitle-like transcript; champagne appears in another episode, but this breakfast does not establish drunkenness.

title: Too Hot to Handle, season 3 episode 3: group confrontation over conflicting claims
inspected: Full episode transcript, later rule-break announcement and argument about what was said to two women.
finding: The conflict circles the disputed wording of earlier conversations: accusation, denial, correction, simultaneous interruption, renewed denial. Third parties and replayed footage escalate rather than settle the exchange.
quote: I didn't lie about it. I just didn't say nothin'.
label: Evidence
writer_takeaway: When accused, have a character narrow the meaning of one verb and make the others repeat the contested claim.
limitations: Edited reality TV with producer-controlled revelation and cutaway evidence; no reliable full-conversation timing.

title: Temptation Island, season 1 episode 11: final bonfire breakup
inspected: Full episode transcript, final bonfire sequence with a betrayed partner's statement and response.
finding: One partner alternates direct accusation with self-reproach; the other begins with an old endearment, which is rejected twice before the substantive explanation resumes. Hurt does not appear as a neat sequence of setup, rebuttal and resolution.
quote:
Don't call me that.
Don't call me that.
label: Evidence
writer_takeaway: Let a familiar term of affection become unacceptable in the middle of a rupture, and allow repetition without new information.
limitations: Heavily edited reality TV; host enforces turn-taking, and previews and confessionals are intercut. Separate hand-segmented 18-turn final-bonfire excerpt in measure_media_turns.py has median 3 words/turn and 13/18 (72.2%) turns of 4 or fewer words; this is not an episode-wide estimate.

title: Temptation Island, season 1 episode 11: host-mediated decisions
inspected: Full transcript, earlier bonfire decision segment with both partners choosing to leave alone.
finding: A speaker cushions the final decision with fillers, respect and residual affection; the host then restates the choice for clarity, forcing a blunt answer after a qualified one.
quote: I still respect you. I still love you.
label: Evidence
writer_takeaway: Let an emotionally decisive answer arrive only after hedges and a concrete follow-up question.
limitations: Edited reality TV; formal host prompts and fixed choice architecture are unlike private couple talk.

title: Bachelor in Paradise season 9 episode 6 recap
inspected: Deadline's episode recap paragraphs describing Kat and Tanner's breakup, plus Jess and Blake's pre-date conversation.
finding: The recap describes a partner naming a specific hurt before the other explains an alternative connection; after separating, each gives the friend group a different face-saving account. Another pair recognizes their own prior wish to explore options while still feeling rejected when the other does it.
label: Evidence
writer_takeaway: Make the public retelling of a disagreement different from the private one, especially when both want to save face.
limitations: Journalist's paraphrase, not a transcript; edited reality TV; no claims about exact turn length or wording.

title: Frankenbites 101: Reality TV Editing
inspected: Audio editor Vanessa Flores's article on assembling interview snippets and altering breath timing, crossfades, stretch and pitch.
finding: The editor describes joining fragments from different parts of an interview into grammatically coherent sentences and manipulating timing and inflection to hide seams; apparent fluency or timing on a reality show therefore cannot be treated as a raw conversational measurement.
label: Evidence
writer_takeaway: Use edited TV for social beats and conflict loops, not for a model of untouched everyday timing.
limitations: Practitioner article about reality production generally, not proof any particular episode here was frankenbitten.

title: Where Should We Begin?: Impotent is No Way To Define a Man
inspected: HappyScribe transcript, especially 06:30-13:10 discussion of touch, timing, explicit request and feedback.
finding: The pair distinguish desire for contact from whether this moment is welcome. Under therapist prompting, one asks for a specific touch, then tries lighter pressure, tip-of-finger contact and a simple report that it feels nice; uncertainty about preference is allowed before trying.
quote: I think I like it lighter.
label: Evidence
writer_takeaway: For consensual novelty, make preference discovery a sequence of small requests and feedback, not a fluent speech about desire.
limitations: Anonymized couple in a one-time, edited therapy session; machine transcription may err; avoid identifying or importing personal histories into fiction.

title: Modern Love: Un-Marry Me!
inspected: HappyScribe transcript, opening reported domestic nap-time dispute and 05:28-06:39 reported marital conversation.
finding: In the interviewee's recollection, a charged household disagreement starts with a missed routine and an immediate practical objection; later, a relationship-defining announcement provokes repeated attempts to pin down what a new term means, not instant mutual understanding.
quote: Detaching? What does that even mean?
label: Evidence
writer_takeaway: When a partner introduces a new relationship label, let the other ask what it changes in practice.
limitations: A public person's retrospective account and narrator-mediated podcast, not a recording of the couple's original private exchange; machine transcription.

title: Modern Love: Myha'la's Relationship Advice? Get in a Fight
inspected: HappyScribe transcript, first six minutes of host interview about early messages and attraction; episode introduction to discussion of arguments.
finding: A host asks for a remembered specific question; the guest admits she cannot recall it, then reconstructs feelings and mundane details such as an interview request, timing and a bottle of wine. A recollection of attraction is far messier than a perfect flirt exchange.
label: Evidence
writer_takeaway: Let a recollection fail on a factual detail and detour through ordinary logistics before returning to emotion.
limitations: Hosted, edited interview, not the couple talking to each other; automated transcript misrenders names and capitalization.

title: Turn Towards Instead of Away — Gottman Institute
inspected: Gottman Institute article definition and examples of bids, turning toward and missing a bid.
finding: A bid for attention may be a smile, wink or request for help rather than a direct relationship check-in; missing it leaves less room for repair than an overt response, according to the article.
label: Evidence
writer_takeaway: Hide an 'are we okay?' question inside a small bid and show whether the other notices it.
limitations: Research-informed guidance and author interpretation, not a transcript of a particular couple; reported study percentages are not independently audited here.

title: How to Fight Smarter: Soften Your Start-Up — Gottman Institute
inspected: Gottman Institute article contrasting a blame-heavy opening with a specific complaint and request, including guidance after defensiveness.
finding: The examples distinguish describing an observable problem and need from judging a partner's character; even an 'I feel' sentence can function as blame if it smuggles in 'you never.' A reassurance after a defensive response can redirect the discussion.
quote: I don't feel heard right now.
label: Evidence
writer_takeaway: Give a conflict opener one observable grievance and a request, and let defensiveness still be possible.
limitations: Prescriptive examples, not records of naturally occurring talk; good practice should not make every character sound therapeutic.

title: R is for Repair — Gottman Institute
inspected: Gottman Institute article definition of repair attempts and examples of mutually agreed interruption gestures.
finding: A repair can be any action, even silly, that stops escalation; the article's example is a couple agreeing on a playful physical signal, while warning that an uninvited 'calm down' is unhelpful.
label: Evidence
writer_takeaway: Give the established couple one idiosyncratic, mutually understood de-escalation cue rather than a stock quip.
limitations: Prescriptive relationship writing with an anecdotal couple example, not a controlled transcript; a cue may fail depending on context.

title: Before Sunrise (1995): train conversation
inspected: Film dialogue transcript from train meeting through extended imagined TV-show digression.
finding: Questions about language and travel elicit an overlong false start about speaking French, and a mundane trip report unexpectedly expands into an elaborate TV-show idea; the other person interrupts and mocks its premise without ending the connection.
label: Inference
writer_takeaway: Let one partner take a long, peculiar detour and let the other puncture it with a short, concrete objection.
limitations: Fully scripted and performed; coherent digression and elegant callbacks are writerly craft, not evidence of everyday frequency.

title: Before Sunrise (1995): Vienna invitation
inspected: Film dialogue transcript at the train's Vienna stop, invitation, practical questions and hesitant acceptance.
finding: A wish to keep talking meets questions about what they would do and how travel would work; the inviter offers the option of the next train but then gives an improbably complete imagined-future monologue to persuade her.
quote:
What would we do?
I don't know.
label: Inference
writer_takeaway: Borrow the uncertain practical follow-up and explicit exit option, not the perfectly structured persuasion speech.
limitations: Scripted contrast only; not evidence of real-world consent practices or average speech patterns.
